name: Transformers
works_with: Python 3.10+ with PyTorch 2.6+, and many training and inference tools such as vLLM, SGLang, DeepSpeed and llama.cpp
short: Hugging Face's Python library for running and training text, vision, audio and multimodal models from the Hub.
what: Transformers holds the model definitions for a large range of open models, so the same model works across many training and inference tools. Its `pipeline` API runs text generation, speech recognition, image classification and more in a few lines. The README says there are over 1M model checkpoints on the Hugging Face Hub you can use with it.
who: Developers and researchers who want to run or fine-tune open models in Python. The README says it isn't a toolbox of building blocks for neural nets, and that for generic training loops you should use another library like Accelerate.
needs: Disk space and a network connection for model downloads

steps.title: Make a virtual environment
steps.text: The README shows venv. It shows uv too.

steps.title: Run a first pipeline
steps.text: The model downloads and caches the first time you run this.
steps.code:
from transformers import pipeline

pipeline = pipeline(task="text-generation", model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B")
pipeline("the secret to baking a really good cake is ")

steps.title: Or install from source
steps.text: For the latest changes. The README warns the latest version may not be stable.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git
cd transformers

# pip
pip install '.[torch]'

try.label: From the README
try.text: With `transformers serve` running, chat with a model from the command line: `transformers chat Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`

watch: Pipelines download model weights from the Hugging Face Hub the first time. Some models are large.
The README says the example scripts may not work out of the box for your use case.
Installing from source gets you the newest code, which may not be stable.
